Kalmia Control Quest

Six missions on tonight's three lessons. Each one starts with a real problem at Kalmia Coffee Roasters: you try first, then the rule appears — the rule you just discovered. Nothing here is graded: the XP and badges are only there to show your path.

Problem first, first principles second: a decision follows written rules, a control carries two independent labels, and a match starts from the risk and ends with a list of gaps.

How to play

Open a mission, read the problem, make your move. When you finish a mission, the rule box opens and the related slides are one click away. The Lecture, Slides, Lab 4 preview, Cards and Words tabs are always open — use them whenever you are stuck.

Progress is stored only in this browser (local storage) and never sent anywhere.

Mission 1 — Four doors

ProblemNadia Roy has twelve ranked risks and four possible decisions: reduce, transfer, avoid, accept. For each risk, read the four facts on the card and choose the decision. The written policy appears after each answer.

The rule you foundA treatment decision follows written rules, not opinions. TP-1: avoid what is not essential. TP-2: accept a LOW risk. TP-3: accept a MEDIUM risk only when no low-cost control exists, for 12 months, in writing. TP-4: reduce every other risk. TP-5: add TRANSFER when the reduced risk has impact 4 or 5 and an insurer or a contract can cover it. TP-6: no HIGH or CRITICAL risk ends with ACCEPT only. Kalmia: REDUCE 10 (four with TRANSFER), AVOID 1, ACCEPT 1. Due dates come from the priority class: P1 7 days, P2 30, P3 90, P4 365.

Mission 2 — What is it made of?

ProblemTwelve Kalmia controls. Ignore when they act and answer one question only: is the control a written rule that people apply, hardware or software, or something that acts on the premises?

The rule you foundThe category says what the control is made of: administrative (a written rule, procedure, training or agreement applied by people), technical (hardware, software or configuration), physical (premises, power, temperature). CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 splits administrative into managerial and operational.
▣ slide 24▣ slide 27

Mission 3 — When does it act?

ProblemThe same twelve controls, a new question: does the control act before the event (it stops it), during the event (it reveals it) or after the event (it limits the damage and restores)? Each answer places the control in the 3 × 3 grid.

The rule you foundThe function says when the control acts: preventive before the event (it mainly lowers the likelihood), detective during the event (it shortens the time to detect, so it mainly lowers the impact), corrective after the event (it limits the damage and restores, so it lowers the impact). Category and function are two independent axes: all nine cells of the grid can be filled.
▣ slide 25▣ slide 27▣ slide 29

Mission 4 — Break the chain

ProblemR-01: a ransomware group sends a phishing message, uses the shared NAS-01 administrator password and the flat network, encrypts the shares and stops order processing for days. Seven controls are planned. Where does each one act on this chain?

The rule you foundMatching starts from the risk, not from the tool. Read the scenario statement: threat source, threat event, risk factors, asset, consequence. Preventive controls act on the event and the risk factors, the detective alert on the asset, the corrective controls on the consequence. Kalmia cannot act on the threat source itself.
▣ slide 38▣ slide 39

Mission 5 — Gap hunter

ProblemBefore the plan goes to Nadia Roy, every treated risk must pass four matching rules. For each risk, read its row of the traceability matrix and tick the rules that fail.

    The rule you foundM1: every reduced risk has a new control. M2: a HIGH or CRITICAL reduced risk has two different functions. M3: every risk factor has a control or is listed as a gap. M4: an avoided risk has the control that carries out the avoidance. Kalmia's matrix gives five findings in four risks — the Lab 4 work list. Without the rules, the plan would have looked complete.
    ▣ slide 41▣ slide 42

    Mission 6 — Lab 4 pilot

    ProblemFive gaps are left in Kalmia's plan. For each one, choose the control that closes it — the same work you will do on your own register in Lab 4.
    The rule you foundA gap is closed by a control that acts on the missing risk factor or adds the missing function — not by a second control of the same kind, and not by insurance. Then the mapper runs again: zero findings, or a written explanation for each one left.

    Lab 4 — Risk treatment and prevention plan (Integrative Project, Part 4) — summary only

    • What you will build: Kalmia's risk treatment and prevention plan, starting from your own Lab 3 register.
    • Decisions: one treatment option per risk with the policy rule that justifies it (tonight's Lesson 1).
    • Controls: the classified control catalogue (Lesson 2) and the traceability matrix with the four matching rules, with every gap closed or explained (Lesson 3).
    • Later parts: cost versus benefit, continuity measures and residual risk (Class 13), preventive measures and their own risks (Topic 7).
